nodes.content: Design an incremental cross-module optimizer that preserves optimization benefits while maintaining sound cache reuse under symbol interposition.
requirements: Match clean-build semantics under dependency changes, dynamic symbol interposition, and mixed optimized/unoptimized modules.
For single-module edits, halve full-LTO rebuild time while keeping runtime within 5% of full LTO.

nodes.content: Cache optimized function partitions by dependency and symbol-resolution fingerprints; inline only provably nonpreemptible definitions, retaining calls into unoptimized modules.
Which symbol-resolution and visibility facts must enter partition fingerprints to prevent stale inlining after weak-definition or interposition-policy changes?
Recording prevailing-definition identity, linkage strength, visibility, and interposition policy while forbidding preemptible inlining prevents stale reuse across weak/DSO changes.
Enumerate resolution inputs, key affected partitions, and compare incremental versus clean builds across weak, DSO, and mixed-mode edits.
Run InterposeMatrix-48, toggling weak winners, DSO preload, visibility, and unoptimized callers; compare cached binaries against clean-build traces.
InterposeMatrix-48 found zero trace mismatches; all 12 weak-winner changes invalidated affected partitions while unrelated partitions remained cached.
Adopt resolution-aware partition keys and prohibit preemptible inlining, since InterposeMatrix-48 showed zero clean-build trace mismatches.
Implement the adopted resolution-aware partition cache and benchmark EditBench-30 single-module edits for rebuild time and runtime versus full LTO.
IncrementalLTO v0.1 contains resolution-aware partition caching, nonpreemptible-only inlining, and EditBench-30 rebuild-time and runtime reports.
Run DependencySweep-64 with transitive callee edits across optimized/unoptimized modules; compare cached traces and partition invalidations against clean builds.
DependencySweep-64 found three clean-build trace mismatches when transitive callee edits bypassed partition fingerprints and reused stale inline bodies.
Extend resolution-aware partition keys with Merkle-hashed transitive inline-body dependencies, invalidating affected callers while retaining nonpreemptible-only inlining.
Implement Merkle dependency invalidation; rerun DependencySweep-64 and InterposeMatrix-48, then benchmark EditBench-30 rebuild time and runtime against full LTO.
Patch IncrementalLTO v0.1 with transitive inline-body Merkle hashes, then rerun DependencySweep-64 and InterposeMatrix-48 against clean builds.
IncrementalLTO v0.2 adds transitive inline-body Merkle keys and emits partition invalidation logs for DependencySweep-64 and InterposeMatrix-48.
Does transitive invalidation halve EditBench-30 rebuild time while keeping runtime within 5% of full LTO?
On EditBench-30, v0.2 cuts median single-module rebuild time by at least 50% with runtime slowdown below 5%.
Benchmark IncrementalLTO v0.2 on EditBench-30 against full LTO, measuring median rebuild speedup, runtime slowdown, and clean-build trace equivalence.
EditBench-30: v0.2 cut median rebuild time 54%, increased runtime 3.1%, and matched clean-build traces in 30/30 cases.
Repeat EditBench-30 with five randomized edit orders and mixed optimized/unoptimized modules, measuring median rebuild savings and runtime versus full LTO.
Five shuffled mixed-mode EditBench-30 runs cut median rebuild time only 42% versus full LTO, below the hypothesized 50%.
Caching fingerprinted resolution summaries alongside Merkle keys yields ≥50% median mixed-mode rebuild savings on EditBench-30 with under 5% runtime slowdown.
Profile v0.2 on shuffled EditBench-30, attributing rebuild time to resolution-summary recomputation versus partition compilation.
Optimized-only EditBench-30 edits retained 54% median rebuild savings versus full LTO; resolution-summary recomputation consumed 18% of mixed-mode time.
Cache fingerprinted resolution summaries in v0.2; rerun five shuffled mixed-mode EditBench-30 orders, measuring full-LTO-relative rebuild savings and runtime.
Five shuffled mixed-mode EditBench-30 runs saved 47% median rebuild time despite cached summaries; runtime slowdown remained 3.2%.
Measure resolution-summary hit rates and rebuild savings across mixed-mode EditBench-30 edits, stratified by symbol churn.
Low-churn mixed-mode edits saved 53% median rebuild time with 91% summary hits; high-churn edits had 39% hits.
Retain summary caching for low-churn edits, but optimize high-churn resolution because mixed-mode savings remain 47% overall.
Maintain a per-symbol resolution dependency graph; recompute summaries only for changed bindings and dependents, preserving interposition-aware invalidation.
How can the resolution graph detect weak-winner and DSO preload changes without invalidating partitions that depend on unrelated symbols?
Fingerprint link-time candidate sets and preemptibility policy per symbol; retain dynamic calls and invalidate only dependents of changed bindings.
Implement per-symbol candidate fingerprints, preserve preemptible calls, and test weak-winner/preload changes for clean-build equivalence and localized invalidation.
Run InterposeMatrix-48 with per-symbol fingerprints; compare clean-build traces and unrelated-partition invalidations after weak-winner and DSO-preload changes.
InterposeMatrix-48 matched 48/48 clean-build traces; weak-winner changes invalidated only dependent partitions, and DSO preloads preserved dynamic dispatch.
Mutate weak candidates and visibility across mixed-mode DependencySweep-64; compare invalidation reachability and preemptible-call dispatch against clean builds.
DependencySweep-64 found 2/64 trace mismatches: weak aliases in unoptimized modules changed bindings without invalidating canonical-symbol dependents.
Tracking weak-alias-to-canonical edges across unoptimized modules and fingerprinting resolved target candidates prevents stale bindings without unrelated invalidation.
Add weak-alias canonical edges, rerun DependencySweep-64 and InterposeMatrix-48, then measure shuffled EditBench-30 savings.
Add canonical weak-alias edges to the mixed-mode resolution graph; rerun DependencySweep-64 and InterposeMatrix-48 against clean-build traces and invalidation logs.
DependencySweep-64 and InterposeMatrix-48 matched clean-build traces in 112/112 cases; weak-alias edits invalidated dependents only.
Adopt canonical weak-alias tracking: it fixes the two mixed-mode mismatches while retaining localized invalidation and 112/112 clean-build matches.
Integrate canonical weak-alias tracking into IncrementalLTO v0.3; benchmark shuffled mixed-mode EditBench-30 rebuild savings and runtime against full LTO.
IncrementalLTO v0.3 includes canonical weak-alias dependency edges, per-symbol resolution invalidation, and shuffled mixed-mode EditBench-30 benchmark reports.
Schedule invalidated partitions across eight workers, retaining unaffected cache entries and rechecking symbol-resolution fingerprints before final link.
Implement eight-worker partition scheduling with final-link fingerprint checks; benchmark shuffled EditBench-30 and verify clean-build traces under concurrent edits.
Run five shuffled mixed-mode EditBench-30 orders with eight-worker v0.3, measuring rebuild savings, runtime slowdown, and clean-build trace agreement.
EditBench-30 eight-worker report records rebuild savings, runtime slowdown, and clean-build trace agreement across five shuffled mixed-mode orders.
Do eight-worker runs close the 47%-to-50% mixed-mode rebuild gap without exceeding 5% runtime slowdown or introducing trace mismatches?
Eight-worker v0.3 achieves at least 50% median mixed-mode rebuild savings, under 5% runtime slowdown, and 150/150 clean-build trace matches.
Analyze the eight-worker EditBench-30 report for median rebuild savings, runtime slowdown, and clean-build trace matches across 150 edits.
Eight-worker EditBench-30 saved 52% median rebuild time, slowed runtime 3.3%, and matched clean-build traces in 150/150 edits.
Stratify the eight-worker EditBench-30 report by symbol churn; stress concurrent weak-winner and DSO-preload changes against clean-build traces.
Concurrent-churn EditBench-30 replay matched only 148/150 clean-build traces, versus 150/150 in the initial eight-worker run.
Pin immutable resolution snapshots and retry links on epoch changes, targeting 150/150 clean-build matches, ≥50% rebuild savings, and <5% slowdown.
Add epoch-pinned resolution snapshots, retry changed epochs, and rerun concurrent-churn EditBench-30 plus weak/DSO clean-build comparisons.
Implement epoch-pinned resolution snapshots and retry stale links; replay 150 concurrent-churn EditBench-30 edits against clean builds.
Epoch-pinned replay matched 150/150 clean-build traces, saved 51% median rebuild time, and incurred 3.4% runtime slowdown.
Run concurrent weak-winner and DSO-preload changes in InterposeMatrix-48, checking epoch retries and clean-build traces across mixed-mode links.
InterposeMatrix-48 exposed 1/48 clean-build mismatches because unoptimized weak-winner publications bypassed epoch increments, leaving stale bindings.
Keep epoch-pinned snapshots, but block release until unoptimized weak-winner publications increment epochs; replay passed EditBench-30 but failed InterposeMatrix-48.
Epoching unoptimized weak-winner publications restores 48/48 interposition matches and 150/150 churn matches with ≥50% rebuild savings, <5% slowdown.
Epoch all weak-winner publications, including unoptimized modules; repeat InterposeMatrix-48 and concurrent-churn EditBench-30 with clean-build and performance checks.
Epoch unoptimized weak-winner publications; rerun InterposeMatrix-48 and concurrent-churn EditBench-30, checking traces, rebuild savings, and runtime.
After weak-winner epoching, InterposeMatrix-48 matched 48/48 traces; churn EditBench-30 matched 150/150, saved 50.5% rebuild time, and slowed runtime 3.5%.
Repeat 150 concurrent-churn EditBench-30 edits with fresh seeds and randomized unoptimized weak-winner publications; verify traces, rebuild savings, and runtime.
Fresh-seed EditBench-30 matched 150/150 traces, saved 48% rebuild time, and slowed runtime 3.6% versus full LTO.
Retain weak-winner epoching for correctness, but defer release: fresh-seed rebuild savings fell to 48%, below the 50% target.
Batch weak-winner publications into atomic epoch commits; rerun fresh-seed EditBench-30 for ≥50% rebuild savings, <5% slowdown, and trace equivalence.
IncrementalLTO v0.4 batches weak-winner updates into atomic epoch commits and includes fresh-seed EditBench-30 trace and performance reports.
Reuse unchanged partitions across epoch-retried links, validating their dependency fingerprints against the committed snapshot before final linking.
Can snapshot-validated retry reuse recover fresh-seed rebuild savings above 50% without admitting stale partitions after concurrent weak-winner changes?
Reusing partitions only when Merkle and resolution fingerprints match the committed epoch yields ≥50% rebuild savings and zero trace mismatches.
Add committed-epoch validation for retry reuse; benchmark fresh-seed EditBench-30 and verify weak-winner/DSO clean-build traces.
Add committed-epoch fingerprint checks to v0.3 partition caching; benchmark fresh-seed EditBench-30 rebuild savings, runtime, and clean-build traces.
Fresh-seed EditBench-30 with committed-epoch retry reuse saved 52% median rebuild time, slowed runtime 3.6%, and matched 150/150 traces.
Stress v0.3 retry reuse with concurrent weak-winner flips and DSO preloads in InterposeMatrix-48, comparing traces and reused-partition fingerprints.
InterposeMatrix-48 found 1/48 trace mismatches: versioned weak aliases shared one resolution key, reusing a stale partition after winner flips.
Key versioned weak aliases by name, version, and canonical target before snapshot validation; expect ≥50% savings and zero mismatches.
Separate versioned weak-alias keys, validate retry reuse against committed snapshots, and rerun InterposeMatrix-48 plus fresh-seed EditBench-30.
Patch v0.3 with versioned weak-alias keys; rerun InterposeMatrix-48 and fresh-seed EditBench-30 against clean builds and full LTO.
Versioned keys restored 48/48 InterposeMatrix-48 trace matches; fresh-seed EditBench-30 saved 51% rebuild time with 3.6% runtime slowdown.
Combine v0.4 atomic commits with versioned retry keys; stress InterposeMatrix-48 and EditBench-30 for trace equivalence and rebuild savings.
Combined v0.4 passed 48/48 InterposeMatrix-48 and 150/150 EditBench-30 traces; median rebuild savings reached 53%, runtime slowdown 3.7%.
Adopt versioned retry keys with v0.4 atomic commits: they fix the stale-alias mismatch while delivering 53% savings and 3.7% slowdown.
Gate versioned-key, atomic-commit v0.5 on DependencySweep-64 and InterposeMatrix-48 trace matches, plus fresh-seed EditBench-30 ≥50% savings and <5% slowdown.
IncrementalLTO v0.5 release candidate includes versioned alias keys, atomic epoch commits, snapshot-validated retry reuse, and correctness/performance gate reports.
